meta.description: Cross-method decision tree and runnable helpers for calling and reconciling hits in pooled CRISPR screens.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All audit values are traceable to fresh real HAP1 files or explicitly seeded synthetic fixtures; no fabricated study or clinical claims were produced.

practice_boundaries.detail: All outputs are screen-level research analysis and contain no individual diagnosis, treatment recommendation, or patient data.

methodological_ground.detail: The audit confirmed design-matched method selection, score-direction correction, fixed-seed BAGEL guidance, and sensitivity plus specificity of the comparison guard.

code_usability.detail: All four shipped Python files py_compile clean; the three shipped CLIs and example completed on fresh real or synthetic inputs.

functional_suitability.note: The decision tree, reconciliation rules, thresholds, references, and runnable helpers cover the stated use cases; the heading 'Run All Five' overstates the three-method command beneath it.

reliability.note: The Skill now names real failure modes and its comparability guard demonstrated both sensitivity and specificity; malformed input schemas still surface pandas errors rather than a purpose-specific message.

performance_context.note: The 191-line SKILL.md uses three targeted references and three scripts, keeping loaded context proportional to the task.

agent_usability.note: Method selection, thresholds, warnings, confidence tiers, and stop conditions are explicit and tested; the five-versus-three wording is a minor source of avoidable ambiguity.

human_usability.note: Natural example prompts and concise prerequisites support discovery; direct CLI error messages could better identify required columns.

security.note: No secrets, network calls, shell interpolation, or destructive operations occur. Input table columns are not validated before indexing.

maintainability.note: Reference split and scripts separate concerns. The two-method example and three-method helper retain parallel threshold logic, though fresh real-data results agree.

agent_specific.note: Precise triggers, progressive disclosure, composition links, and escape hatches are strong; the two minor static ambiguities prevent full marks.

key_strengths: All nine regression cases and two independent new cases executed fresh against the exact requested worktree tip.
Real HAP1 runs confirm threshold agreement, score-direction handling, single-guide protection, BAGEL rerun interpretation, and comparison-guard sensitivity and specificity.
The split references and runnable scripts keep the central SKILL.md compact while retaining executable evidence.
The source CLIs compiled clean and the synthetic fixtures exercised both NTC-calibrated z-score and truly matched three-method consensus paths.

recommendations.title: Rename the five-method consensus heading
recommendations.problem: The section titled 'Run All Five on the Same Data' invokes a three-method MAGeCK+BAGEL2+drugZ script and discusses two-to-three-method consensus.
recommendations.root_cause: An older broad-consensus heading survived after the runnable scope was made explicit.
recommendations.fix: Rename the heading to 'Run two or three methods on the same data' or add the two omitted methods with equivalent runnable integration.

recommendations.title: Validate required input columns before indexing
recommendations.problem: The shipped pandas scripts index required columns directly, so a malformed input produces a raw KeyError rather than a named input-contract error.
recommendations.root_cause: CLI argument parsing validates paths but not table schema.
recommendations.fix: Add a small required-column check in each script that lists missing columns and states the expected schema before pandas indexing.
